facts: Separate nonpurulent cellulitis, drained abscess and surgical necrotizing infection; MRSA coverage is risk selected. Do not routinely give antibiotics to uninfected dermatitis.
pending_scenarios: Diabetic-foot/osteomyelitis and chronic suppression; all severe allergy alternatives; IV vancomycin AUC protocols.

pathways.title: Crohn's Disease and Ulcerative Colitis Diagnosis and Management
facts: Perianal abscess requires drainage; antibiotics are reserved for spreading cellulitis, systemic infection or immunosuppression. Routine luminal IBD is not an indication.
pending_scenarios: Fully sourced perianal-abscess antibiotic selection/doses/duration; fistula biologic combination scope.

pathways.title: Acute Pancreatitis Diagnosis and Management
facts: Do not give prophylactic antibiotics for sterile pancreatic necrosis. Infected necrosis needs agents penetrating necrosis, culture-directed care and source-control assessment.
pending_scenarios: Carbapenem-sparing/resistant-pathogen alternatives; intervention timing and full organ-specific pathways.

pathways.title: Lyme Disease Diagnosis and Treatment
facts: Use disease-specific dosing and age guidance; the old blanket under-eight doxycycline prohibition is superseded for eligible short-course Lyme indications.
pending_scenarios: Full cefuroxime and pediatric neurologic/arthritis branches; refractory arthritis response thresholds; pregnancy selection.

pathways.title: Pleural Effusion Evaluation and Management
facts: Distinguish infected pleural collections from noninfected effusions; use cultures and source control.
pending_scenarios: Hospital-acquired/resistant pathogens, oral step-down and individualized duration.

pathways.title: CAP Severity Assessment and Antibiotic Therapy
facts: Choose outpatient versus nonsevere inpatient versus severe CAP first; resistant-pathogen add-ons require risk assessment, cultures and de-escalation.
pending_scenarios: Complete short-course stability/exclusion checklist; all pediatric, allergy and resistant-pathogen definitive courses.

pathways.title: AOM Diagnosis and Antibiotic Management
facts: Distinguish AOM from noninfected effusion; use observation only in eligible children with reassessment. Severe beta-lactam allergy is not a blanket TMP-SMX indication.
pending_scenarios: Infants <6 months; high-risk allergy/failure beyond loaded options; pediatric kidney/liver dysfunction.

pathways.title: HIV Diagnosis, ART Initiation, and Initial Regimen
facts: Use organism, IgG, CD4, viral load and ART status to distinguish prophylaxis from active treatment.
pending_scenarios: MAC prophylaxis/treatment; Toxoplasma active treatment, alternatives/G6PD, full high-dose renal/dialysis tables.

pathways.title: C. difficile Classification and Antibiotic Treatment
facts: Initial nonfulminant, recurrence and fulminant/ileus treatment are separate; enteral and IV vancomycin are not interchangeable.
pending_scenarios: Pediatric CDI, microbiota-based therapies and extended-pulsed fidaxomicin; rectal administration protocol.

pathways.title: Gonorrhea, Chlamydia, and Syphilis Treatment
facts: Separate uncomplicated STI, PID, disseminated disease and neurosyphilis. Pregnancy and treatment failure have distinct decisions.
pending_scenarios: Gonorrhea aminoglycoside allergy option; recurrent/resistant trichomoniasis/BV; congenital syphilis, full pregnancy follow-up and all allergy protocols.

pathways.title: Sickle Cell Disease Complications, Hydroxyurea, and Acute Management
facts: Penicillin prophylaxis does not replace urgent fever or acute-chest evaluation. NHLBI acute-chest care includes IV cephalosporin plus macrolide and supportive/specialist management.
pending_scenarios: Full pediatric acute-chest combination dosing, febrile sepsis and penicillin-allergy prophylaxis.

pathways.title: Sepsis-3 Definition, Diagnosis, and 1-Hour Bundle
facts: Do not give prophylactic antibiotics for sterile pancreatic necrosis. Infected necrosis needs agents penetrating necrosis, culture-directed care and source-control assessment.
pending_scenarios: Carbapenem-sparing/resistant-pathogen alternatives; intervention timing and full organ-specific pathways.

pathways.title: Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis Diagnosis and Management
facts: Establish bacterial eligibility before prescribing; observe selected uncomplicated adults with reliable follow-up.
pending_scenarios: Pediatric treatment; high-dose resistance risk; severe allergy/complication and failure branches.

pathways.title: Acute Pharyngitis — Group A Streptococcus Diagnosis and Treatment
facts: Treat confirmed GAS; assess allergy phenotype and local resistance before a macrolide/clindamycin alternative.
pending_scenarios: Cefadroxil/clarithromycin branches; full pediatric organ guidance.

pathways.title: Cirrhosis Complications — Varices, SBP, Hepatic Encephalopathy, and HCC Surveillance
facts: Ascitic PMN >=250 cells/mm3 can support SBP despite negative culture; do not require positive culture. Cirrhotic GI bleeding is a conditional prophylaxis indication.
pending_scenarios: Nosocomial/resistant SBP; complete albumin eligibility/dosing and primary-prophylaxis thresholds.

pathways.title: Acute Bronchitis — Diagnosis and Antibiotic Avoidance
facts: Routine uncomplicated bronchitis does not warrant antibiotics; pertussis treatment and eligible PEP are separate indications.
pending_scenarios: Complete infant/pediatric and nonmacrolide regimens; current timing/PEP eligibility.

pathways.title: Acute otitis externa
facts: Use the exact otic product and assess delivery; persistent symptoms require reassessment.
pending_scenarios: Necrotizing otitis externa; wick/aural toilet details and all alternative drops.

pathways.title: Suspected infective endocarditis — diagnostic classification
facts: A narrow historical trial regimen does not define empiric or organism/valve-specific endocarditis care.
pending_scenarios: Current native/prosthetic-valve, enterococcal, staphylococcal and culture-negative pathways.

pathways.title: Acute rheumatic fever — diagnostic assessment
facts: GAS eradication is distinct from prolonged secondary prevention after acute rheumatic fever.
pending_scenarios: Secondary benzathine dose/interval/duration by age, carditis and residual valve disease; alternatives.

pathways.title: Upper GI bleeding — risk assessment
facts: Ascitic PMN >=250 cells/mm3 can support SBP despite negative culture; do not require positive culture. Cirrhotic GI bleeding is a conditional prophylaxis indication.
pending_scenarios: Fully structured SBP treatment plus albumin, resistant/nosocomial SBP and full high-risk primary prophylaxis eligibility.
